title: Trim becomes a tool and the recording window retires
goal: A recording now opens in the ordinary editor, but only if you switch it on, because the small video window is still the only place you can trim, crop, save or export one. Finish the move: make trimming a tool you pick in the editor, give the editor the save, the export and the revert the old window had, and then take the old window away so there is one way to open a recording and not two.
notes:
SPLIT OUT of a-document-can-have-time on 2026-09-20, by the runner that built the first half. Read docs/design/video.md 7 before anything else: it says exactly what is still standing and why.

WHAT LANDED, so this task does not rebuild it. PhotonzCore gained MovieRef and Layer.movie (MovieClip.swift): which recording a layer plays, an id plus a picture size plus a length, no pixels and no path. PhotonzDocument.recording(_:name:cutList:) opens a recording as an ordinary document with one clip layer. drawn(atTimeMS:) swaps each clip's ImageRef for the frame at that moment, so DocumentRenderer draws video without one line of change. App side: MovieLibrary (id to URL), MovieDecoder (an actor owning the AVAssetImageGenerators) and MovieFrameFetcher (decode, file in ImageStore, 16 frame budget) in MovieFrames.swift; EditorState+Time.swift holds the playhead, play, pause, step and scrub; the transport and the draggable playhead are in MotionStripView.swift. Window routing is in PhotonzApp.EditorRootView, gated on Experiments.shared.recordingIsADocument.

WHY THE FLAG IS OFF. Trim, crop, save, export and Revert to Original all live in VideoEditorState and none of them work on the document path. Turning it on today would take them away from anybody who opened a recording. So the flag is off, the old window is still the default, and this task is what turns it on.

WHAT TRIM IS, already settled and drawn: docs/design/video-surface.md 10, UX-PATTERNS D20, pages/video-shell.html block 05, pages/comp-video.html 08. Crop and Trim become a ToolGroup so no slot moves; the letter c belongs to the FAMILY (ToolGroup.tools(answeringTo:)) rather than to either tool, which means Tool.crop.shortcutKey becomes nil and anything printing Crop's key reads it off the family. The family's ring is filtered to the members this document can use before it is walked, which is the one thing ToolGroup does not do today. trimBeforeSession, resetTrimSelection, commitTrim and cancelTrim are kept as they are, renamed to the tool's session.

THE WALKS drive through action ids (videoTrimDone, not a button called Done), so the ids survive the move; what does not survive is every step that opens the separate window and reads its strip. PlaytestHarness already branches openSampleRecording on the flag and adopts an EditorState when it is on, so the walks have somewhere to land.

SAVE IS THE FIRST THING TO FIX, and there is a trap in it. The first build of this set had the window adopt the .mp4 as its sourceCaptureURL, which is 'Save writes the flattened picture back over the file this came from' — Command S would have replaced an eight second recording with a PNG of one frame of it. That is gone: EditorState.isRecordingDocument now makes saveAffordance report nothingToSave, which dims Save and stops the close sheet asking a question nothing can answer. The cost is that styling a clip and closing loses it silently. Two things have to be decided when this is picked up: what Save MEANS for a recording document (the recording window's Save writes the trimmed mp4 through VideoAssetCommit, and that is probably still the right answer), and whether a recording document can be written as a .photonz at all, since MovieRef deliberately carries no path and a package would reopen with a clip whose frames cannot be found.
acceptance: Save stops being dimmed: a recording opened as a document can be saved, and saving it writes the recording rather than a picture of one frame of it. Today Save reports there is nothing to save, and closing the window loses any styling without asking
Trim is a tool in Crop's slot: C picks it, C again swaps, and it is offered only when the document has a duration. No slot in the tool bar moves
Trimming puts handles on the clip's bar in the timeline, both up without hover, with the frames outside the in and out drawn as spare at each end with their durations

The session ends on one glass capsule shaped like Crop's: readouts and Reset in its settings half, then Cancel, then a primary button reading Trim. Return trims, Escape cancels, and no Reset/Cancel/Done row survives
A recording that is one clip and has never been edited opens with the clip picked and Trim in hand, so trim-and-send is still drag a handle, Return, export
Save, Save a copy, export and Revert to Original all work on a recording opened as a document, and each is checked in the audit

The eleven walks that drive the shipped trim flow (trim-*, undo-while-trimming, save-is-live-after-a-trim, close-a-trimmed-recording, the two tutorial-trim-a-recording ones) are rewritten against the new surface and pass
next-a-recording-is-a-document is on by default in Next, or is deleted and the document path becomes the only path
VideoEditorState, VideoEditorView, TrimTimeline and PlaybackScrubber are deleted, and the audit says so

The tutorial copy moves with the chrome: TutorialGuides.swift step 'keep-whats-between' at .video(.trimDone) says "Done throws the ends away and leaves you the middle", which is both the wrong button name and against the model, since a trim leaves the frames outside the in and out in the document

log.note: ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building. (1) The mock puts the handles in the TIMELINE and the Cancel/Trim capsule over the CANVAS, two places at the bottom of the window. Kept, because the thing being bounded really is the bar, but picking Trim now OPENS the timeline if it is shut: a tool whose handles are behind a closed dock is a tool that does nothing. (2) The mock says Crop gives its letter to the family. That takes C off Crop in the ungrouped bar, which is what Current ships and what Next shows with tool groups off, and that bar reads Tool.crop.shortcutKey with no family to fall back on. Built the other way: both members answer to c and the family has no key of its own, which behaves identically and leaves Current alone. (3) 'The spare at each end, with its duration' has nowhere to be drawn once a trim has shortened the document: the frames are before time nought. Answered by laying the clip out at FULL length for the length of the session (PhotonzDocument.openedForTrim, pure, nothing written), so the ruler, the bar and the playhead all cover everything the trim could give back. (4) Cut the mock's separate handle-preview idea: the canvas already draws the frame under the playhead and dragging a handle moves the playhead to it.

SHIPPED, half the task. Trim is a tool: Tool.trim in Crop's slot as ToolGroup.bounds (no slot moves, C swaps, offered only where the document has a duration), ClipTrimSession + applyTrim/openedForTrim/clipToTrim/opensWithTrimInHand in PhotonzCore with 20 tests, EditorState+Trim for the session, handles and spare on the clip's bar in MotionStripView, one glass capsule (readout, Reset, Cancel, Trim) in EditorView.trimActionBar, Return commits and Escape cancels through CanvasKeys. A fresh one-clip recording opens with the clip picked and Trim in hand. Tutorial 'keep-whats-between' rewritten off 'Done throws the ends away'. Scripts/test.sh green, 8554 tests. trim-is-a-tool-walk passes with six real window captures; the nine runnable trim/crop/recording/tool walks still pass (three refused for the locked screen, unrelated). Commit 33e1cbc3. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-20-trim-is-a-tool.json. ACCEPTANCE: items 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 are done. Items 1, 6, 7, 8 and 9 (Save/export/revert on the document path, the eleven walks rewritten, the flag on, the four files deleted) all wait on the decision card, because every one of them needs to know what Command S means for a recording somebody has also drawn on.

LEFT ROUGH, no task filed, nothing a person hits today. (a) The trim capsule counts In and Out from the start of the recording rather than from the document's clock. Identical for a recording that is one clip, which is every recording there is; it would disagree with the ruler for a clip sitting later on a timeline, and there is no way to make one yet. (b) Nothing on the CANVAS says a trim is live, where Crop darkens what it is about to lose. Trim's gesture is in the timeline, so this may be right rather than missing; it is in the audit for the user to react to. (c) Crop's slot flyout now stacks three kinds of row (the family, the aspect locks, Resize Image); also in the audit. (d) Overflow: at a narrow window the crop slot's stand-in still registers a plain C that picks Crop, so the swap is not reachable from the chevron menu. One press, one tool, never wrong, just less than the wide bar offers.

Trim is a tool and it is shipped (commit 33e1cbc3, audit 2026-09-20-trim-is-a-tool). The rest of the task — Save, export and Revert to Original on the document path, the eleven walks rewritten, the flag on by default and the four old files deleted — all turn on one question that is now a card on the dashboard: what Command S should do to a recording you have also drawn on. Nothing else in the task can be decided without it.

Design review 2026-09-21, folded from the 2026-09-20-trim-is-a-tool audit so it is not lost when the card is answered: the Crop slot flyout now stacks three kinds of row in one list (the Crop/Trim family at the head, then Crop's four aspect locks, then Resize Image). UX-PATTERNS has a vocabulary for a tool family in a slot and one for a tool's options; it has no rule for a list that is both plus a command. Whoever finishes this task should either group them visibly or say in video-surface.md why one flat list is right, so the next tool that joins a slot has an answer.

Half of the 'Save, export and Revert to Original all work on a recording opened as a document' item is done as of 2026-09-21: EXPORT works. Shift-Cmd-E on a document with time opens the video sheet (VideoExportDialog) and writes a real video of what plays, with the same three formats and presets the recording sheet offers, behind next-export-the-video (on by default in Next). See queue/audits/2026-09-21-video-export.json and docs/design/video.md section 8. Save and Revert are still the old window's, and the Command S card is still the thing this task waits on.

Found while making the recording window's button row read correctly (the-video-bar-s-buttons-say-what-they-do-in-the), and left here because this task owns that window's fate. The Export BUTTON in that row is the only Export in the app that does not go through the Export sheet: VideoEditorView.exportMenu builds its own Menu of 'Export MP4… / Export GIF ▸ / Export HEIC ▸' and never reads Experiments.shared.recordingExportSheetEnabled, while EditorCommands does read it and gives File ▸ Export… (⇧⌘E) and Video ▸ Export… the sheet. So with the flag on — which is its default in Next — the same word means two different things depending on which one you press. Read from the code and from recording-export-sheet-walk (which reaches the sheet through the videoExportSheet action, never through the button); NOT reproduced by pressing the button, because a walk cannot open a SwiftUI Menu in that window. Whoever moves save and export into the editor should make sure only one Export survives.
